settingsInfra.bypass.heading: Pause the prompts
settingsInfra.bypass.hint: A relief valve for incident work: for this long, anything set to Ask runs straight through. Block is NOT affected — to change that you have to edit the table above, where it is visible.
settingsInfra.classDesc.context-switch: Changes the account, region or cluster later commands run against.
settingsInfra.classDesc.destructive: Deletes a resource. Cannot be undone.
settingsInfra.classDesc.read: Fetches data to look at. Changes nothing.
settingsInfra.classDesc.write: Changes a resource’s configuration or state.
settingsInfra.heading: Infrastructure command permissions
settingsInfra.intro: Every aws, terraform and kubectl command — whether an agent calls it or you click it in the AWS screens — passes the table below before it runs. This is the only place it can be changed, and each change leaves a line in the Ledger.
settingsInfra.matrix.confirmReset: Reset the whole table to the AWOG defaults?
settingsInfra.matrix.confirmUnblock: This is the strongest fence in the design: delete commands on a production account are currently BLOCKED outright, with no way to approve them. Lowering it means a delete on production will start appearing as a prompt you can allow. Change it anyway?
settingsInfra.matrix.heading: Permission table
settingsInfra.matrix.hint: Pick per command class and account kind. When two sources disagree, the stricter one wins.
settingsInfra.modeDesc.ask: Shows an approval card and waits for you.
settingsInfra.modeDesc.auto: Runs immediately, no prompt. Still recorded in the Ledger.
settingsInfra.modeDesc.block: Does not run, and no button can approve it.
settingsInfra.noEngine: No engine connection, so the active policy could not be read. Reopen the app and try again.
settingsInfra.prod.empty: No account marked yet. An account with a pinned id counts as normal.
settingsInfra.prod.heading: Accounts treated as production
settingsInfra.prod.hint: An account whose id AWOG does not know counts as production BY DEFAULT — not knowing where you are means assuming you are somewhere dangerous. That is why the PRODUCTION chip can appear on a personal profile: run the identity check for that profile in the AWS screens to pin its id, then add the ids that really are production here.
settingsInfra.vouched.heading: Vouched binaries
settingsInfra.vouched.hint: CLI paths outside the standard directories that you confirmed yourself. Add one from the AWS screens when AWOG reports a missing binary; here you can only revoke.
